question: The LCM of the numbers 15.4 and 0.006 is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the number of decimal places: **15.400** and **0.006**.

Remove decimals and find **LCM** of **15400** and **6**.

LCM(15400, 6) = **46200**.

Place the decimal back after 3 places (as in 15.400): **46.200**.

**∴ The correct answer is 46.2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e51f29a852a8ad89dc90ba08844448e15c962f4a78f3f04a484df0e4c80427d7.png] 

**Given values:** Numbers are **15.4** and **0.006**.

**Formula:** LCM of Fractions = **LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators**

⇒ Convert decimals to simplified fractions:

⇒ 15.4 = 154/10 = **77/5**

⇒ 0.006 = 6/1000 = **3/500**

⇒ LCM(77, 3) = 77 × 3 = **231**

⇒ HCF(5, 500) = **5**

⇒ Required LCM = 231 ÷ 5 = **46.2**

**∴ The correct answer is 46.2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF of Fractions

LCM = LCM(Numerators) ÷ HCF(Denominators). HCF = HCF(Numerators) ÷ LCM(Denominators).

Decimal LCM Rule

Always equate the number of decimal places by adding trailing zeros before calculating LCM or HCF as integers.

Product Rule

For any two numbers a and b, **a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**.</p
